summary: Lampus or Lampos (Ancient Greek Λάμπος, "glitter, shine") was a Trojan elder, son of King Laomedon and Strymo (or similar), brother of Priam, and father of Dolops. Homer seats him with Priam among the elders at the Scaean gates.
etymology: Ancient Greek Λάμπος / Λάμπος from λάμπω "to shine, glitter."

sections.heading: Elder of Troy
paragraphs: As Laomedon's son Lampus sits among the Trojan gerontes who watch Helen from the wall. His son Dolops, skilled with the spear, fights and falls in the Iliad — a Laomedontid branch beside Priam's house.

The name also belongs to horses (Eos', Helios', Hector's team, Diomedes' mares) and to minor humans (a son of Aegyptus; a Theban ambusher). The atlas id lampus-trojan is the Trojan elder and Dolops' father alone.
